facts.text: Founded 1818 by brothers Seth and Zebulon Leavenworth as an Ohio River port, Leavenworth grew into a bustling shipping hub.
Leavenworth served as Crawford County seat from 1843 until 1896, when county records were moved after a Supreme Court ruling.
Pearl button factories dotted Leavenworth, cutting mussel shells into discs that were sanded and shipped to Massachusetts before plastic buttons ended the industry after WWII.
The first newspaper of Crawford County, The Crisis, began publishing in Leavenworth in 1839, marking the town’s early press history.
Old Leavenworth, the original town on the Ohio River floodplain, was almost completely destroyed by the 1937 flood, the most devastating in the valley’s history.
A bluff overlooking the Ohio River, part of the Indiana Ridge, rises behind Leavenworth and faces directly across the river toward Kentucky.
